description:
USER REQUIREMENT (2026-10-24, A): the PPI-bug collection must be EASY TO ADD TO AND REMOVE FROM -> build it as the REGISTRY of docs/parser-review-s525.md §7 (one row per bug, id = catalogue §, kind token|structure|source|lexer-dies, when/fix/repro/tokens/ppi.fixed_in; consumers = the 1a engine, the canary test with the STALE DETECTOR, the upstream report, the catalogue; the skip-registry pattern).  The c1 checker session designs the row schema against the real 38 and files the kind split.  The ENDGAME it serves is review §8.

RULED (USER, 2026-10-24): Option 3 (perl compiles, PCL translates the optree) is OFF -- an exact perl version at transpile time or one parser per perl version is unrealistic, and the compiled-code cache would freeze the compile-time environment (perl folds on it; review §4 Option 3 risk 2).  The spike below is CANCELLED; this task now carries Option 1 in the revised order.  Cadence: ONE of the two slots per round (the perf slot shape), the other slot keeps the correctness / board batches.  NOT pushed to later: Parser2 grows +12k lines / 90 days, every corner case landed in the old shape is migration surface.

STEP 0 -- TWO INERT CHECKERS (one session each, zero emission change, corpus-diff IDENTICAL by construction):
  c1 expect-state checker: walk PPI significant tokens left to right carrying toke.c expect (XSTATE / XTERM / XOPERATOR / XBLOCK / XREF); for every token whose PPI class contradicts the state, LOG (file, line, token, PPI class, expected class) over the four populations; compare the log against the ~35 repair passes: which repairs it predicts, which tokens it flags that no repair touches (new PPI bugs or checker errors -- probe vs perl), which repairs it does NOT predict (a second state needed?).  Deliverable: the table + the PPI-class x expect-state -> correct-class table read off toke.c yyl_* handlers (yyl_slash, yyl_leftcurly, yyl_lt, yyl_percent, yyl_ampersand, yyl_star, yyl_hyphen, yyl_question).
  c2 binder dual-run (s379 Direction A step 1, pad.c rule: visible from the statement AFTER the declaration, OUTER = capture): one early walk assigning every my/our/state/signature param a binding id and resolving every use (code + interpolated via InterpScan) to it; at every call of _binding_at / _ref_shadowed / _block_captures_name assert agreement, DIE with both verdicts on disagreement (PCL_BINDER_CHECK=1); run over corpus + Pl/t + board.  Every disagreement = a live bug or a design error -- probe vs perl, file.

STEP 1 -- 1a ONE expect-state repair pass replacing the ~35 repair passes and all 18 re-serialize-and-reparse sites: re-lex a contradicting span with PPI::Tokenizer (the fragment_doc pattern), re-tag, continue; `{` in XSTATE/XBLOCK takes yyl_leftcurly lookahead (word/string then , or => = anon hash).  Bar: the 38 canary rows (misc-fixes-02.t + ppi-bug-report.t) hold; corpus-diff IDENTICAL; passes 69 -> fewer; re-parse sites 18 -> 0.  2-3 sessions.

STEP 2 -- 1c the binder PORTS, newest consumer first (requalifier -> capture gate + promoter -> span -> state/cond/shadow/emb), each deleting its private resolver; the SWEEP is the gate (name-resolution change, #296 rule); then name-choice moves to emission.  Bar: scope-walk implementations 18 -> 1; Calc.pm transpile 3.7 s -> < 1.5 s; corpus-diff IDENTICAL per port.  5-7 sessions.

STEP 3 -- 1b ONE keyword-class table (prototype("CORE::name") + ~30 syntax keywords) + ONE extent rule per class (FUNC parens; UNIOP one term to the comparison level; LSTOP to the next same-level or/and/xor or ); FUN0 nothing; a user sub takes its prototype class).  Bar: handle_subcalls 1,811 -> < 600; corpus-diff IDENTICAL.  2-3 sessions.

FILLERS: rename Pl/Parser.pm live halves (PrePass / Facts); close the four-kind text seam (use/require, loop-modifier statements, BEGIN, use constant).

STANDING RULE (effective now, s379 §8 restated): no new scope walk, no new rename suffix family; once c1 exists, no new repair pass -- a PPI mis-lex becomes a row in its table; until then a new PPI bug gets catalogue section + report row + canary in the SAME commit (principle 13; the report lags the catalogue by §5 and §32-§38 today).

RESIDUES: r1 three stale ppi-upstream-bugs.md § citations (_restore_signature_gid §24->§32, _brace_glob_slot_symbol §24->§27, _repair_term_initial_complement §20->§21); r2 Config -11/-12 identical codes; r3 Parser.pm naming + text seam; r4 nine PPI documents per transpile (the binder is the fix, not a cache).

CANCELLED (kept for the record): the Option 3 spike S1-S5 (op census, version delta, compile-time input census, 40-op slice, eval seam).  Measured before the ruling: ops 396 (5.26.3) -> 400 (5.32.1) -> 422 (5.40.3), none removed; core B::Deparse supports only its own perl; perl folds `use constant D => $ENV{D}; print "x" if D` to an unconditional or absent print, $^P NOOPT does not prevent it.

=== STEP 1d ADOPTED (Fable, s526, 2026-10-24, from docs/codegen-review-s526.md §12) ===
The code-generation review found the compiler's structural debt entirely in Parser2's STATEMENT lowering and recommended no separate program: its options C1-C3 join THIS program as step 1d.
  C1 -- the statement CLASSIFIER (target-architecture §2.2): ONE `Stmt::classify($ppi_stmt, $env)` returning kind + pre-split spans; `_lower_block_1` / `_lower_stmt` / `_lower_compound` switch on kind and never index token arrays; the s525p expect-state tables (Pl/PPIExpect.pm) are its data.  IDENTICAL emission.  Bar: `_lower_block_1` 1,188 -> under 300 lines; `isa`/`content` shape tests outside the classifier 52 -> 0; corpus-diff IDENTICAL; gate + the sweep.  2-3 sessions.  Runs right after 1a (the classifier is what makes 1a's tables consumable).
  C2 -- close the v1 TEXT seam one statement kind per session, biggest first: `local` (337 corpus statements; `p-local` from v1's 1,068-line `_process_local_declaration`), `use`/`no`/`require` (411; the phase model already has the form), `BEGIN` (147), signatured subs with defaults/slurpy placeholders (89; generalise `sig-classic`), loop-modifier statements (47; generalise #3375's desugar), the tail (22); then DELETE `Pl::CLForm::raw`, `fallback_parser`, the 33 `_process_*`, the 53 text heads.  Each kind is an EMISSION change (generation bump, sweep, corpus-diff explained per file).  Bar: seam statements 1,058 -> 0 on the review's 120-file corpus (`PCL_V2_SEAM_CENSUS=1`); `is_raw` calls 160k -> 0 per module; Pl/Parser.pm 13,562 lines -> its pre-pass/facts half only.  4-6 sessions, interleaved with the 1c ports (each kind deletes v1 code the ports would otherwise carry).
  C3 -- facts on BINDING IDS = 1c's consumer side: VarAnnotator and the facts keyed by the binder's binding id; `_let_bound_vars` (51 uses, 12 save/restore sites) -> the binder's scope query; one context encoding.  Bar: `_let_bound_vars` 51 -> 0; corpus-diff IDENTICAL.
  The parser slot's ORDER from here: 1a (the expect-state REPAIR pass consuming the tables + the registry) -> C1 -> the 1c ports (requalifier first: docs/binder-dual-run-s525.md §6, fixes #3800 #3801 #3804 by construction) interleaved with C2 kinds -> 1b.  Fillers for any slot: C4 the void-position bind as a Kind-A gate (`p-void-ctx` 8,636 -> after; measure first; bench bar), C5 #75's constructor macros with the next generation bump, C6 name the `use integer` arithmetic heads (host leaks 31 -> 17), C7 rule-10 splits (`gen_funcall_form` 853 lines by builtin family).  R4's code half (`p-setf` to one arm) follows from C1 + C2 (the review's §2b store census is its measure: `p-setf` 483 -> toward 0).

=== C2 kind 1: local (s533c) ===
(Opus 5.5, 2026-11-04, resumed s534 2026-11-05.)  The `local` STATEMENT leaves the v1 text seam: Pl::Stmt::local_shape gives the record's sub-kind (delete / glob / arylen / elem / globdyn / deref / items / seam / loopmod -- v1's old branch order as data, with the spans), and Parser2::_local_plan_<lk> builds { opens, inner, value } as CLForm trees with v1's heads, argument order and temporaries; _local_nest puts the block remainder inside the innermost open.  ir-spec §7.2.
CENSUS BEFORE (D0, scratch/s533c/local-census.tsv, s533a's 2,047-file list = perl-tests, everyday, lib, perl t/ + core lib, the board's t/): 2,651 `local` statements -- items 1,525 (magic var 718, `$` scalar 434, `@`/`%` 159, list 185, `local our` 29), elem 829, glob 207, delete 27, deref 21, `my (…) = delete local` 20, globdyn 12, arylen 3 (+ 7 truncated census rows the standalone re-parse could not classify).
AFTER: every family structured.
